description: A pure CALCULATION node — the inverse of Points to Graph. Graph JSON in, point MATRICES out: every edge as its start point, its end point and its thickness, plus the node positions. This is the bridge INTO the matrix chain.
instructions:
A value-only node: a graph as JSON in, matrices out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing — wire the outputs into a Math Engine, or into Matrix / Vector nodes.

WHY IT EXISTS: Points to Graph is the bridge OUT of the matrix chain (positions → connectivity). This is the way back IN. A graph JSON is an OBJECT, so wiring it into a Math Engine variable gives you an inert string — nothing to compute with. Split into matrices, an edge list is ordinary linear algebra: `Gb - Ga` is the edge-vector list, `normalize(Gb - Ga)` its directions, `len(Gb - Ga)` its lengths, and a pairwise test on `vcat(Ga, Gb)` recovers which endpoints are the same node.

OUTPUTS, all in the same anchor-relative METRES as Space Geometry's val-points, so they wire straight back into Polygon / Network:
• `a` — M×2, each edge's START point (from_node_id).
• `b` — M×2, each edge's END point (to_node_id). Row i of a and b is edge i, which is exactly what Points to Graph's Pairs mode consumes, so the pair round-trips.
• `thickness` — M×1 metres per edge, 0 where the edge carries none. Set Thickness / Merge Graph / Graph Geometry publish it; a flow can then stroke each edge at its own width.
• `nodes` — N×2, the node positions in the graph's own order.
• `nodeCount` / `edgeCount` — the two counts, for driving a loop bound or a numeric param.
An edge naming a node the graph doesn't define is skipped, so the three edge outputs always agree row for row.

SKIP OPENINGS (on by default): edges tagged `type: "opening"` — what Graph to Openings carves for a door or a window — are left out, matching what Mitered Join does with them. Turn it off to get every edge including the openings.

NODE IDENTITY is NOT carried: matrices hold numbers, not ids. Two edges meeting at a node have IDENTICAL coordinates in their a/b rows, so recover the junction with a coordinate test — `min(where(le(D2, tol*tol), T(k), BIG), 'rows')` over the pairwise distance matrix of `vcat(a, b)` gives every endpoint the row index of its first coincident partner, i.e. a canonical node id per endpoint. See Workflows/Operations/mitered_join_with_math.json.
